At about 2 p.m. July 16, some 30 boatmen in employ
of the members of the Shanghai Municipality Association
of Owners of Lighters for Transportation of Coal and
Stone (405 Tientsin Road), were taken into custody by
representatives of the Inland Boatmen's Trade Association
(sponsored by the Japanese), at the mouth of the Soochow
Creek, where the latter association has recently established
a temporary office on a boat afloat with one Japanese and
one Chinese as its personnel. The arrest was made because
of their failure to register with the Inland Boatmen's
Trade Association, and the arrested persons were released
after three hours' detention.

It is learned that Chow Wen-ziang (周文祥), committee
member of the Inland Boatmen's Trade Association, and
Feng Ts-sing (馮志新) of the Shanghai Citizens' Society,
have repeatedly approached the Shanghai Municipality
Association of Owners of Lighters for Transportation of
Coal and Stone in an attempt to persuade the latter to
register. Despite the offer of the former to reduce the
deposit money and membership fees by 50%, and the promise
to grant the committee members similar positions in the
Inland Boatmen's Trade Association with a monthly allowance
of $100 each, the committee members of the Shanghai Muni-
cipality Association of Owners of Lighters for Transportation
of Coal and Stone have refused to conform to the demand made
by the Inland Boatmen's Trade Association.

An association known as the Inland Waters Cargo Boat Association
sponsored by the Ta Tao Government has been formed with offices
in Shanghai for the express purpose of collecting registration
fee and tax from all cargo junks operating on the Soochow Creek.

The Head Office of this association is located on Wucheng
Road, Chapei, whilst a Branch Office was opened on the 13th
May 1938 at No. 793 Soochow Road.

Further enquiries made at No. 793 Soochow Road ascertained
that this office has ceased functioning since the 20th June
1938, all boatmen intending to register being referred to the
Head Office, Wucheng Road.

The Branch Office is under the charge of one named Mao Tse
Ming (馬濟民), he being responsible to one named Zung Tuh Ming
(陳德銘) in charge of the Head Office, Zung Tuh Ming being in
turn under a Japanese executive.

When detectives visited No. 793 Soochow Road, Mao Tse Ming
was absent, however, it was ascertained from an assistant named
Sung Wei Loong (孫為龍) that before any cargo boat can proceed
along the Soochow Creek, the owner of same, first had to register
with the above association, the fee being by tonnage, $1.00 per
ton for large cargo boats, whilst a flat rate of $5.00 was charged
for a boat of five tons or under.

In addition to the above a registration fee of $1.00 per boat
is levied, this being payment for a registration flag.

一个名为“内河货船协会”的组织已由大道政府（Ta Tao Government）赞助成立，并在上海设有办事处，其明确目的是向所有在苏州河运营的货运舢板收取注册费和税款。

该协会的总办事处位于闸北武进路，而分办事处于1938年5月13日在苏州路793号开设。

在苏州路793号进行的进一步调查查明，该办事处自1938年6月20日起已停止运作，所有打算注册的船夫均被指引至武进路的总办事处。

分办事处由一名叫马济民（Mao Tse Ming）的人负责，他向负责总办事处的陈德铭（Zung Tuh Ming）汇报，而陈德铭又受一名日本主管领导。

Under the pretext of obtaining passes for boat owners the
"Inland Waters Cargo Boat Association" is compelling our members to
pay security. If the security is paid to ensure the safe transport-
ation of cargo, the boatmen can make direct arrangements with the
owners of goods; the assistance offered by a third party is un-
called for. Hence there is no reason whatever for collecting
security from our members.

As for the membership fee, the Association can only persuade
lighter owners to become its members and should not resort to
forceful measures to achieve this object. In the interest of
public safety the Council is requested to kindly bring this matter
to the attention of the Japanese Consul-General and the Military
authorities concerned, to promptly depute some officers to make
a thorough investigation into this matter and to prohibit the
unlawful collection of fees so that our members may continue to
pursue their avocation in peace.

“内河货船协会”借口为船主获取通行证，强迫我们的会员缴纳保证金。如果缴纳保证金是为了确保货物运输安全，船主可以直接与货主安排；无需第三方提供协助。因此，完全没有理由向我们的会员收取保证金。

至于会员费，该协会只能劝说驳船船主成为其会员，而不应采取强制措施来实现这一目标。为了公共安全，恳请工部局将此事项提请日本总领事和有关军事当局注意，迅速派遣官员对此事进行彻底调查，并禁止非法收费，以便我们的会员能够继续和平地从事职业。

HEAVY TAXES BEING LEVIED ON INLAND WATER BOATS
After the outbreak of hostilities, traffic by
railway and highway became interrupted and the Soochow
Creek was the only waterway from Shanghai to the interior.
Rice, vegetables, fruits, meat, fuel and other daily
necessities are being transported to Shanghai from the
interior by boats which in turn carry piece goods, sea
products, salt, sugar, foreign goods, bean oil, paper,
cigarettes and paper to the interior.

Shanghai Municipal Administration, has formed an Inland
Boat Owners' Association. This Association has issued
an order instructing that boats plying in inland waters
must first pay a membership fee and the locdah of the boat
must pay 50 cents, while every boatman must pay 20 cents.
A security of $1 is to be collected on every ton of goods
on a boat, and a transportation fee of 20% of the value
of the transported goods has to be paid.

The present work of the Society is principally to assist boatmen in their registration with the Dah Dao City Government. It usually takes a boatman five or six days or even more to have his boat registered with the Shipping Control Office of the Dah Dao City Government, whereas only one or two days are sufficient when the assistance of the Boatmen's Lien Nyi Society is solicited. The branch office of the Society, situated at 793 Soochow Road, is purposely established for receiving members who wish to solicit the assistance of the Society in getting registered with the Dah Dao City Government.
